title: How can we shorten before we multiply?
description: Twelve sevenths is multiplied by five twenty fourths. On the board the twelve and the twenty four are both divided by twelve before anything is multiplied, so only small numbers are left to work with. Keeko raises the doubt of dividing only the twelve.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide a top and a bottom by the factor they share, before multiplying. Watch for students who divide only one of the two numbers, which changes the value of the fraction.

source: Multiply 12/7 × 5/24 and give the product in its lowest form
video_script.why: A learner sees that a top and a bottom with a shared factor can be shortened before the multiplication, which keeps the numbers small.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own example, twelve sevenths and five twenty fourths
video_script.anchor: the product of twelve sevenths and five twenty fourths, written as one fraction
video_script.wrong_move: divides only the twelve by twelve and leaves the twenty four, which changes the value
video_script.payoff_line: Twelve sevenths times five twenty fourths is five fourteenths
video_script.fraction_reading: twelve sevenths, five twenty fourths, five fourteenths, five one hundred sixty eighths
maths_rules: 5 and 14 share no factor, so 5/14 is in lowest form
the slip: (1 × 5)/(7 × 24) = 5/168, which is not equal to 5/14
video_script.design: One product of two fractions written as one fraction. The twelve and the twenty four are linked and shortened in one colour; the rest stays plain.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the two fractions 12/7 and 5/24 with a times sign between them

marks.pose: the two fractions arrive with a times sign between them
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the product

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about multiplying two fractions.
<bookmark mark='pose'/>Multiply twelve sevenths by five twenty fourths, and write the product in its lowest form.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the product in its lowest form?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 12/7 × 5/24 written as (12 × 5)/(7 × 24) and left unworked; the 12 and the 24 have a soft outline

marks.rule: the product is written as tops over bottoms
marks.big: the twelve and the five sit on top, the seven and the twenty four below
marks.share: the twelve and the twenty four are outlined
marks.keep: an equals sign appears between a fraction and the same fraction shortened

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Two fractions are multiplied by multiplying the tops and multiplying the bottoms.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Here that gives twelve times five on top, and seven times twenty four below.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Before multiplying, we can look for a top and a bottom that share a common factor.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>A fraction keeps its value when its top and bottom are divided by the same number.

marks.given: the two fractions are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the two fractions are twelve sevenths and five twenty fourths.

marks.find: the words To find and the product are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find their product in its lowest form.

marks.write: the product is written with the tops together over the bottoms together
marks.same: tops and bottoms are bracketed in two pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write the product as twelve times five over seven times twenty four.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Tops go with tops, and bottoms go with bottoms.

beats.on_screen: cancelling: 12 and 24 are linked; 12 ÷ 12 gives 1 and 24 ÷ 12 gives 2; the working shows (1 × 5)/(7 × 2)

marks.link: the twelve and the twenty four are linked by a line
marks.left: the one and the two replace them

beats.colours: the shared numbers in the accent colour
beats.moves_through: the 12 and the 24 change into 1 and 2
narration: <bookmark mark='link'/>Step two, twelve and twenty four share the factor twelve, so divide both by twelve.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Twelve divided by twelve is one.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Twenty four divided by twelve is two.

marks.mult: the tops and the bottoms are multiplied
marks.low: a tick checks that the top and the bottom share no factor

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step three, multiply what is left, one times five on top and seven times two below.
<bookmark mark='low'/>Five and fourteen share no factor, so the answer is already in lowest form.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Twelve sevenths times five twenty fourths is five fourteenths.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: (1 × 5)/(7 × 24) = 5/168; the bubble is struck through; then the 12 and the 24 are both divided by 12

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows only the twelve changed to one
marks.fix: the twelve and the twenty four are both divided by twelve

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we divide only the twelve, and leave the twenty four as it is.
Keeko gets a product of five one hundred sixty eighths.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>But then the top has changed and the bottom has not, so the value of the fraction changes.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A fraction keeps its value only when the top and the bottom are divided by the same number.
